boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct HPU study environments, ranging from enforced-quiet library areas to collaborative rooms and open academic-building workspaces.

cards.title: Settle Into the Quiet Floor
cards.subtitle: Study carrels and tables among the main book collection
cards.notes: Bring focused reading or writing upstairs; choose a perimeter carrel and observe the floor’s officially designated quiet setting.
cards.short_summary: A quiet library floor lined with individual carrels and tables.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU identifies Smith Library’s third floor as a quiet study area with study carrels, tables, books, and bound journals.
cards.access_notes: Use during Smith Library’s posted hours; the third floor is governed as a quiet study area.

cards.entity_name: Smith Library Lower-Level Collaborative Study Area
cards.title: Build the Group Session Downstairs
cards.subtitle: Collaborative tables near library technology spaces
cards.notes: Take discussion-based coursework downstairs, where collaborative tables support group work without carrying conversation onto quiet floors.
cards.short_summary: The library’s designated setting for active and collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU’s library policy places collaborative study tables, an instruction lab, and lecture halls on Smith Library’s lower level and recommends the area for group study.
cards.access_notes: Use during Smith Library’s posted hours; conversation must remain controlled and headphones are required for audio.

cards.title: Work Beside the Special Collections
cards.subtitle: A quiet second-floor room inside Smith Library
cards.notes: Use one of four individual desks for solo work, or bring a small shared task to the conference table opposite the elevator.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled study room surrounded by archival displays.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU describes the Powell Room as a quiet second-floor study and archive space with a conference table and four individual study desks.
cards.access_notes: Enter through Smith Library during posted hours; displayed collections do not circulate, though librarians can assist with closer examination.

cards.title: Choose a Desk for Quiet Work
cards.subtitle: Third floor of the R.G. Wanek Center
cards.notes: Head to the third floor with an individual assignment; desks, comfortable chairs, computers, and printers support a longer work block.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet-study library on the north side of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU’s current library page describes the Martha Luck Comer Learning Commons as a large quiet-study space with desks, comfortable chairs, computers, and printers.
cards.access_notes: Located on the R.G. Wanek Center’s third floor; consult the live library-hours listing before visiting.

cards.title: Move the Conversation Behind Glass
cards.subtitle: Collaborative room within the Martha Luck Comer Learning Commons
cards.notes: Bring collaborative work into the glass-enclosed room and keep voices low so discussion does not interrupt the Commons’ main quiet area.
cards.short_summary: A separated option for small-group conversation inside the quiet Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU documents a glassed-in Learning Commons area with several group-study tables where quiet conversation is permitted.
cards.source_title: You Spoke. We Heard: Sound Levels in HPU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use during Learning Commons hours; quiet conversation is allowed, but voices must not disturb the main study area.

cards.entity_name: Children’s Library at the Stout School of Education
cards.title: Study With Curriculum Materials Close By
cards.subtitle: Education-focused library in the Stout School of Education
cards.notes: Choose this location for education coursework when juvenile books, teacher resources, or K–12 textbooks need to stay within reach.
cards.short_summary: A subject-focused library for education research and lesson preparation.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU’s current library page states that the Children’s Library at the Stout School of Education houses children’s books, teacher resources, and K–12 textbooks.
cards.access_notes: Check the current library-hours listing before visiting; the collection is specifically oriented toward education materials.

cards.entity_name: Nido R. Qubein School of Communication Library
cards.title: Spread Out at an Oak Table
cards.subtitle: First-floor library with a fireplace
cards.notes: Bring reading, drafting, or a laptop project to the first-floor library; use the solid oak tables when you need a broad work surface.
cards.short_summary: A communication-school library offering tables and fireside seating.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU’s campus study guide identifies a first-floor library in the Qubein School of Communication with a fireplace and solid oak tables.
cards.source_title: Top Places on Campus to Study
cards.access_notes: The university identifies the library on the building’s first floor; building access and operating hours are not stated on the source page.

cards.title: Give the Group a Room of Its Own
cards.subtitle: Professional-style rooms for collaborative work
cards.notes: Use a study room for discussion, interview practice, or shared problem-solving; confirm room availability after entering Cottrell Hall.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed workspaces suited to collaborative assignments and practice.
cards.evidence_claim: An HPU graduate profile specifically documents working in a Cottrell Hall study room and describes its professional-office character.
cards.source_title: Madelyn Mudd Combines Marketing and Theater
cards.access_notes: The official source confirms the rooms but does not state reservation rules or public hours; verify availability on site.

cards.title: Work Beneath the DNA Sculpture
cards.subtitle: Bright lobby seating in Congdon Hall
cards.notes: Set up at a tabletop near the building’s 40-foot DNA sculpture, or choose seating overlooking the biomechanics laboratory.
cards.short_summary: A modern science-building lobby with distinctive study perches.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU’s campus study guide documents tabletops at the base of Congdon Hall’s 40-foot DNA sculpture and seating overlooking the biomechanics lab.
cards.source_title: Top Places on Campus to Study
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to academic-building access; the university source does not publish separate lobby hours or reservation requirements.

cards.title: Plug In Under the Atrium Light
cards.subtitle: Open seating with integrated power outlets
cards.notes: Choose the colorful atrium furniture for laptop work when natural light and an active student-center setting fit the assignment.
cards.short_summary: A bright, open study setting with power built into the furniture.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU’s campus study guide describes Slane Student Center study seating beneath a naturally lit atrium, with built-in electrical outlets in the furniture.
cards.source_title: Top Places on Campus to Study
cards.access_notes: The study area is inside Slane Student Center; check current building access because the source does not specify atrium hours.

warnings: HPU’s live library-hours interface did not expose stable per-location schedules in searchable page text, so cards direct users to check current posted hours.
Coordinates and maps URLs are null because exact room-level coordinates or official direct map links could not be verified.
Several official study-space descriptions are older institutional pages; access notes avoid treating their historical hour claims as current.
Exactly one complete board with ten distinct, under-21-safe cards is included.
